Subsea 7 SA Reports Steady Trade Figures for Second Quarter

Subsea 7 SA, a well-established player in Spain’s oil and gas services and equipment industry, reported routine trade figures for the second quarter of 2024, reflecting steady demand across its portfolio of subsea engineering and construction services. According to company officials, the figures align with internal forecasts and industry expectations for the period.

Turnover for the quarter stood at €116.4 million, a marginal increase from €114.9 million in the first quarter of 2024. The company attributed the performance to ongoing contracts in the Mediterranean, as well as continued maintenance and inspection activities for existing offshore platforms. Chief Financial Officer Marta Rodríguez commented, “We are pleased with the consistency of our operations this quarter. Our teams have maintained high standards in delivery and safety, and our order book remains healthy for the remainder of the year.”

Industry observers note that the stability in Subsea 7 SA’s figures mirrors broader trends in the Spanish oil and gas sector, where gradual recovery in energy demand has supported a stable environment for service providers. “Subsea 7 SA’s results speak to a well-managed operating model and a reliable client base,” said Javier Morales, an analyst at the Iberian Energy Trade Association. “While the sector is not experiencing dramatic growth, it is also free from the disruptions seen in other parts of Europe.”

The Spanish Federation of Energy Workers also welcomed the news. “Consistent activity benefits our members, ensuring stable employment and opportunities for upskilling,” said union spokesperson Eva Martínez.

Looking ahead, the company confirmed it will continue to focus on core operations and invest in workforce training and safety initiatives. No significant changes in project timelines or workforce levels are anticipated for the coming months.
